hero.title: DataTurntable Documentation
hero.subtitle: Standalone user docs for onboarding, operations, troubleshooting, and day-2 platform management.

sections.title: 1) Getting Started
sections.description: Prepare a safe and predictable workspace before changing runtime assets.
bullets: Run initial setup exactly once per environment.
Sign in and verify active tenant context in header.
Confirm API health and dashboard reliability before operations.
Use language/theme controls according to operator preference.

sections.title: 2) Tenant Governance
sections.description: Keep strong isolation and minimal permissions across teams.
bullets: Design root and child tenants by business domain or environment.
Assign users through scoped memberships and explicit roles.
Use diagnostics copy actions for support handoffs.
Avoid wildcard abilities in normal day-to-day accounts.

sections.title: 3) Module Management
sections.description: Treat modules as versioned deployable units.
bullets: Separate IMPORT/PROCESSING/ALERT/EXPORT responsibilities.
Version each change with meaningful tags.
Promote validated versions from non-production to production.
Document intent and dependency impact in module descriptions.

sections.title: 4) Pipeline Operations
sections.description: Operate pipelines with explicit validation and rollback discipline.
bullets: Run test executions after any module or connector change.
Inspect run details, errors, and lineage diagnostics.
Track reliability windows (1h/24h/7d) for drift detection.
Capture root-cause notes for each operational incident.

sections.title: 5) Data Explorer
sections.description: Use built-in analytics to validate and share data quality findings.
bullets: Filter by table, time window, and row limits.
Use trend and distribution widgets to detect anomalies quickly.
Export scoped result sets as CSV or JSON.
Restrict destructive table actions to controlled roles.

sections.title: 6) Alerts and Response
sections.description: Deliver actionable alerts without overwhelming responders.
bullets: Configure channels before enabling rules.
Use severity and throttling to reduce noise.
Monitor delivery states and retry failures promptly.
Define on-call ownership per tenant.

sections.title: 7) Monitoring and Logs
sections.description: Observe the full system with metrics, logs, and infra telemetry.
bullets: Use Grafana overview for uptime and latency trends.
Use infrastructure dashboard for host and container usage.
Use Loki logs to correlate cross-service failures.
In multi-instance Swarm/K8s setups, rely on service discovery metrics.

sections.title: 8) Security and Compliance
sections.description: Apply operational controls that hold up under audits.
bullets: Keep secrets out of git and rotate credentials regularly.
Limit public endpoint exposure to required routes only.
Use tenant isolation for data and operational boundaries.
Record diagnostics snapshots for incidents and change reviews.

sections.title: 9) Backup and Recovery
sections.description: Recover reliably with tested restore procedures.
bullets: Back up PostgreSQL/Timescale volumes and verify restore success.
Store module/pipeline exports in controlled repositories.
Define RPO/RTO by environment and test against targets.
Automate backup health checks and alerting.

sections.title: 10) Troubleshooting Checklist
sections.description: Follow one sequence to shorten mean-time-to-recovery.
bullets: Check API health and authentication first.
Validate tenant context and effective permissions.
Correlate metrics and logs in same time range.
Collect reproducible steps and diagnostics for escalation.

faq.question: Why is a dashboard panel empty?
faq.answer: Most often because datasource bindings or metric labels do not match runtime data. Verify datasource UIDs and label dimensions.

faq.question: Can this docs site run separately from the app?
faq.answer: Yes. It is static and can be served by any web server, CDN, or object storage.
